Treat any failure as "no pull request found", say so and offer the remaining routes rather than stopping.

54	
55	Rename detection is on by default in `git diff`, and `--name-status` reports `R100 old/path new/path`. Lower the similarity threshold with `--find-renames=40%` when a file was moved and edited in the same change.

60	
61	Exclude these and name what you excluded in the scope block. They are machine-authored and carry no interface rules.
62	
63	| Category | Patterns |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| Lockfiles | `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`, `Cargo.lock`, `composer.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock` |
66	| Snapshots and fixtures | `__snapshots__/`, `*.snap`, `*.approved.*`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/` |
67	| Generated output | `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`, `.next/`, `.turbo/`, `.svelte-kit/`, `coverage/`, `storybook-static/`, `*.min.js`, `*.min.css`, `*.map` |
68	| Generated sources | `*.gen.ts`, `*.generated.*`, `*.d.ts` emitted by a build, GraphQL and Prisma client output |
69	| Vendored code | `vendor/`, `third_party/`, `node_modules/` |
70	| Binaries and media | `*.png`, `*.jpg`, `*.webp`, `*.avif`, `*.woff2`, `*.mp4`, `*.pdf` |

75	
76	```bash
77	git diff --name-only "$BASE" <head-ref> -- . ':(exclude)pnpm-lock.yaml' ':(glob,exclude)**/dist/**'
78	```
79

83

85	
86	For `staged`, search with `git grep --cached` and read the index with `git show :path`, including unchanged consumers. For `working`, use the working tree and include untracked consumers.
87	
88	`git grep` searches the working tree by default. Pass the reviewed ref after the pattern, or on a pull request you search a different revision and miss importers the change itself added. Results come back as `<rev>:path/to/file`; read them with `git show`, never the working-tree copy. Pass `-e` when the pattern starts with a dash, such as a `--color-*` token, or git parses it as an option.
89	
90	For a changed token or theme value, search the token name rather than the file, since consumers reference the name and never import it.
91

93

# Scope resolution

How a review target becomes a file list, and the traps that fail quietly and leave the scope block claiming a count it never delivered.

## Default branch

Resolve this only for no-target discovery or a branch/ref comparison. Explicit `working` and `staged` targets use the `HEAD` contract in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md#1-resolve-the-change-scope-first) and skip this section. Pull requests use their own base.

Try `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`. If the ref is missing, ask the remote with `git remote set-head origin --auto` rather than guessing. It needs the network and writes only a ref under `.git`, so it is permitted; note it in Verification. With no remote at all, fall back to a local `main` or `master` and state which base you assumed.

## Targets

Accepted targets are `working`, `staged`, `branch`, `pr <n>`, a bare `<ref>` and an explicit `<a>..<b>` or `<a>...<b>` range. A target token outside that list is a `<ref>`; surrounding instructions are not part of the target.

Diff a branch against the **merge base**, with three dots. Two dots reports every upstream commit that landed on the base branch as part of the change.

But use the dots the user wrote when they wrote a range. `<a>..<b>` compares the endpoints; `<a>...<b>` compares `merge-base(<a>, <b>)` with `<b>`. Rewriting `release..feature` to three dots drops everything between `release` and the merge base, which is often exactly what was asked for. State the resolved range in the scope block.

`git diff HEAD` reports tracked changes only. Any target including uncommitted work must pair it with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`. Otherwise a newly added component is silently dropped from a scope the report claims to cover in full.

## Pull requests

Fetch the head into a remote-tracking ref, `git fetch origin "pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>"`, and review it in place. This works for forks, which `origin/<branch>` does not.

Diff against the pull request's own base, never the default branch by assumption. Read it from `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,baseRefOid` and fetch it if it is not local. A pull request into `release/2.0` diffed against `main` picks up every commit between the two.

Read files at the head ref with `git show refs/remotes/pr/<n>:path/to/file`. Never open the working-tree copy, which is a different revision.

`gh pr diff <n>` is a fine shortcut for the patch text. It gives no way to read unchanged context or expand to consumers, so fetch the ref as well.

**Citations.** Line numbers from a fetched ref need not match the working tree. Cite against the head ref and declare that ref and its SHA in the scope block so the numbers resolve.

**Intent.** The `title` and `body` from `gh pr view` are the stated intent for **Hold the change to its stated intent**. Add the commit subjects when the body is empty.

## Awkward repository states

Three worth handling. Everything else fails loudly at `merge-base`: unrelated histories, a repo with no commits, a moved submodule pointer. Say the base is unresolvable and stop. Never review a range you cannot name.

**Detached HEAD.** Local `working` and `staged` targets still use the current `HEAD` SHA. For a branch comparison or no-target discovery, use the merge base against the default branch and name the SHA, not a branch, in the scope block.

**Shallow clone**, the CI default, where `merge-base` returns nothing. Fetch `--deepen=50`, retry, then `--deepen=200`, then report the scope as unresolvable. Deepening writes to `.git` and not to the working tree, so it is permitted; note it in Verification.

**Mid-rebase or mid-merge**, the one that does not fail loudly. `git diff` succeeds and returns something that is not the change, so the review looks fine and is wrong. Detect it with `git rev-parse --git-path` against `rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, `MERGE_HEAD` and `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`. Do not test `.git/` paths directly, because they are not directories inside a linked worktree. Stop and say the tree is mid-operation.

## Nothing to review

This subsection applies only to no-target discovery. An explicit local target with an empty inventory stays empty; offer another target without remote or merge-base discovery.

For no-target discovery, the tree is clean and `HEAD` is not ahead of the merge base. Gather the facts before asking, so the offer is accurate rather than a guess. They are the current branch, the count ahead of the base, the last commit's SHA and subject and any open pull request from `gh pr status`.

`gh pr status` succeeds when no pull request is open. It omits `currentBranch`, so an empty result is an answer, not an error. It fails outright without `gh`, without authentication and on a repository with no GitHub remote. Treat any failure as "no pull request found", say so and offer the remaining routes rather than stopping.

## Renames

Rename detection is on by default in `git diff`, and `--name-status` reports `R100 old/path new/path`. Lower the similarity threshold with `--find-renames=40%` when a file was moved and edited in the same change.

Review a rename as a move, not a delete plus an add. Everything that survived the move is unchanged code, and only the genuine edits are in scope.

## Excluded paths

Exclude these and name what you excluded in the scope block. They are machine-authored and carry no interface rules.

| Category | Patterns |
| --- | --- |
| Lockfiles | `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`, `Cargo.lock`, `composer.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock` |
| Snapshots and fixtures | `__snapshots__/`, `*.snap`, `*.approved.*`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/` |
| Generated output | `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`, `.next/`, `.turbo/`, `.svelte-kit/`, `coverage/`, `storybook-static/`, `*.min.js`, `*.min.css`, `*.map` |
| Generated sources | `*.gen.ts`, `*.generated.*`, `*.d.ts` emitted by a build, GraphQL and Prisma client output |
| Vendored code | `vendor/`, `third_party/`, `node_modules/` |
| Binaries and media | `*.png`, `*.jpg`, `*.webp`, `*.avif`, `*.woff2`, `*.mp4`, `*.pdf` |

Two exceptions stay in scope. A **font file** added or swapped is a `better-typography` change. An **image** added to a component is a `better-ui` and `better-accessibility` change, through its outline and its `alt` text. Review the code that references them, not the bytes.

Apply the exclusions as pathspecs so the file count in the scope block is the reviewed count:

```bash
git diff --name-only "$BASE" <head-ref> -- . ':(exclude)pnpm-lock.yaml' ':(glob,exclude)**/dist/**'
```

Two traps under-exclude silently. `*.lock` catches `yarn.lock` and `Cargo.lock` but not `package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so cover every suffix in the table. And without `glob` magic, `**/dist/**` needs a literal `/` before `dist`, so it misses a root-level `dist/`. Run the diff with and without the pathspecs and confirm the count dropped by exactly the files you named.

## Expanding to consumers

Use the project's own resolver where one exists, otherwise import paths.

For `staged`, search with `git grep --cached` and read the index with `git show :path`, including unchanged consumers. For `working`, use the working tree and include untracked consumers.

`git grep` searches the working tree by default. Pass the reviewed ref after the pattern, or on a pull request you search a different revision and miss importers the change itself added. Results come back as `<rev>:path/to/file`; read them with `git show`, never the working-tree copy. Pass `-e` when the pattern starts with a dash, such as a `--color-*` token, or git parses it as an option.

For a changed token or theme value, search the token name rather than the file, since consumers reference the name and never import it.

Order the consumers by a rule you can evaluate, so the cutoff is reproducible instead of a guess:

1. **Route and layout entry points first**, whatever the framework treats as a rendered surface: `app/**/page.*`, `app/**/layout.*`, `pages/**`, `routes/**`, `src/views/**`, `*.astro` pages. Everything else only appears inside one.
2. **Then by importer count**, since a component pulled in by twenty files carries more of the change than one pulled in by two.
3. **Break ties by proximity**, same package or feature directory first.

Say plainly if the ordering was arbitrary past a point.

# Surface map

How the changed lines become the domain map: which of the six `better-*` owners the review loads. Classify the lines a hunk adds or removes, on both sides, after [exclusions](scope-resolution.md#excluded-paths). A file's extension or the change's stated intent never decides a row.

## Classify each changed line

A line falls in every row it matches. A domain loads when any changed line falls in a row marked for it.

| Surface | Changed lines that count | Accessibility | Layout | Writing | Typography | Colors | UI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Markup | Rendered elements and components, their attributes (`aria-*`, `role`, `tabindex`, `alt`, `href`, `type`, `disabled`), event handlers on elements, focus calls, and the conditions that choose which element or state renders (loading, empty, error, disabled, open) | load | load | | | | load |
| Copy | A user-facing string added, removed or reworded: text nodes, rendered literals and constants, labels, `alt`, `aria-label`, `title`, `placeholder`, messages, translation catalog entries | load | load when a string is added or gets longer | load | load | | |
| Color | Color values and tokens, `color`, `background`, `border-color`, `outline-color`, `fill`, `stroke`, shadow color, `opacity`, gradients, `color-scheme`, dark-mode queries, color utility classes | load | | | | load | |
| Type | `font-*`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing`, `text-*`, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `hyphens`, `line-clamp`, type tokens and utilities, font files, an element whose type changes heading level or text role | load | | | load | | |
| Box and flow | `display`, `flex*`, `grid*`, `gap`, `margin`, `padding`, sizes and their min/max, `position`, `inset`, `overflow`, `order`, `aspect-ratio`, media and container queries, `dir` and logical properties, spacing tokens and utilities | load | load | | | | |
| Surface and motion | `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, border style and width, `transition`, `animation`, `@keyframes`, `transform`, `cursor`, `z-index`, hover and active styling, scroll and overscroll behavior, icons, SVG and images | load | | | | | load |
| Unclassified | A new file with rendered output, a style declaration or utility class this table does not name, a changed shared primitive or theme object whose rendered effect the diff does not show | load | load | load | load | load | load |

A changed `class` or `className` is classified by the declarations its old and new classes set; read them. A changed design token is classified by its value, and its consumers are reviewed in the domains that value selects: a color token's consumers are checked for contrast, not re-reviewed for layout.

## No UI surface

The change has no UI surface when no changed line falls in any row. Server and API code, migrations, data transforms, tests, build and CI configuration, types, comments, logging and performance work (memoization, caching, request batching, prefetch) qualify when the rendered elements, render conditions, strings, classes and styles stay identical.

Data that flows through an unchanged component is not a surface: a list's contents, a count or an API payload value renders through code this change did not touch. A value the interface shows verbatim, such as a label or message in a constants file, is copy.

A change with no UI surface has no blast radius to expand.

## Ambiguity loads

A line that might fall in a row falls in it. When you cannot tell whether a change reaches rendered output, it is unclassified and all six load. The map can grow during review, when an owner's check reveals a changed surface the map missed; it never shrinks.

## Domain map

Record one row per domain, in the review order, and pass it in the handoff:

| Domain | Load | Changed lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accessibility | yes | `theme/palette.css:14` color token; `src/Sidebar.module.css:8-10` flex direction |
| Writing | no | no copy in the change scope |

A skipped domain's coverage row is `Not reviewed: no <surface> in the change scope`, naming the surfaces whose rows would have loaded it: `no copy`, `no copy or type`, `no color`. It is never `Clear`, which claims an inspection that did not happen.

## 인터페이스 리뷰: `main...HEAD`

이번 브랜치는 UI를 바꾸지 않아서 인터페이스 관점의 지적 사항이 없습니다. 바뀐 건 서버의 카테고리 별칭, 마이그레이션, 테스트뿐입니다. 그래서 `better-interface`로 넘기지 않았고 Approve/Block 판정도 내리지 않습니다. 실제로 검토한 디자인 영역이 하나도 없기 때문입니다.

| 항목 | 값 |
| --- | --- |
| Target | `main...HEAD` (세 점, merge base 기준) |
| Base ref | `af9728aabb6715e9dad27434d33a9e1d5303d9cf` (`merge-base main HEAD`, 현재 `main`과 같은 커밋) |
| Head ref | `feature/merge-ai-categories` @ `33d19b3d652090c7ab2e0aad4b912d6db5ca42ad` |
| Commits | 커밋 1개 (`33d19b3` Merge ai-tools and llm categories into ai), 커밋하지 않은 변경 0개 |
| Files in scope | 3개: `server/categories.ts`, `server/categories.test.ts`, `server/migrations/0007_merge_ai_categories.sql` |
| Excluded | 없음 (lockfile, 스냅샷, 생성물 없음) |
| Surfaces expanded | 없음: UI 표면 없음 |

### 커버리지

| Domain | Evidence inspected | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accessibility | `server/categories.ts`, `server/migrations/0007_merge_ai_categories.sql`, `server/categories.test.ts`: 카테고리 별칭·정규화 목록, 데이터 마이그레이션, 단위 테스트 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |
| Layout | 위와 같음 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |
| Writing | 위와 같음 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |
| Typography | 위와 같음 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |
| Colors | 위와 같음 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |
| UI | 위와 같음 | Not reviewed: no UI surface in the change scope |

**바뀐 UI가 없어서 이번 변경에 대한 인터페이스 지적 사항은 없습니다.**

UI 표면이 없다고 본 이유:

- 바뀐 줄은 서버 쪽 `CANONICAL`/`ALIASES` 슬러그, SQL `UPDATE` 두 줄, 테스트 기대값이 전부입니다.
- 이 슬러그는 `/api/categories` 응답을 통해 화면에 나옵니다(`src/api/feed.ts:20`). 렌더링은 이번에 건드리지 않은 `CategoryChips` 컴포넌트가 맡습니다.
- 그래서 칩 목록에서 `ai-tools`와 `llm`이 사라지는 건 바뀌지 않은 컴포넌트에 들어가는 데이터가 달라지는 것일 뿐입니다. 렌더링되는 요소, 렌더링 조건, 문자열, 스타일은 그대로입니다.
- `Home.tsx`에서 선택된 카테고리는 메모리에만 있는 상태이고 항상 `'all'`에서 시작합니다. 그래서 숨겨진 슬러그가 선택된 채로 화면이 열릴 일도 없습니다.

### 일반 코드 리뷰에서 볼 것

정확성 관련 사항이 하나 있어서, 디자인 판정과 별도로 `/paul-skills:code-review`에서 확인하길 권합니다.

- 마이그레이션이 `categories` 테이블에서 `ai-tools`와 `llm`을 `hidden = TRUE`로 숨깁니다.
- 그런데 `/api/categories`가 `hidden` 행을 실제로 걸러내는지는 이번 diff로는 확인되지 않습니다.
- 걸러내지 않는다면 칩은 그대로 보이는데 눌러도 글이 없는 카테고리가 됩니다.

### 확인 범위

- 브라우저 확인은 하지 않았습니다(요청 범위 밖). 소스만 읽었습니다.
- Git 명령은 읽기 전용만 썼습니다: `diff`, `merge-base`, `log`, `grep`, `show`. 체크아웃, stash, 작업 트리 변경은 없었습니다.
- 중간 상태(진행 중인 rebase/merge) 점검은 권한 문제로 실행하지 못했습니다. 다만 시작 시점의 git status는 clean이었습니다.

tool_input.command: git diff main...HEAD 2>/dev/null; echo ---; for p in rebase-merge rebase-apply MERGE_HEAD CHERRY_PICK_HEAD; do test -e "$(git rev-parse --git-path $p 2>/dev/null)" && echo "mid-op: $p"; done; git ls-files 2>/dev/null
tool_input.description: Show full diff, check mid-operation state, list files
